key_insight: The paper treats each singular-vector channel as a controllable unit of plasticity, selectively updating only the channels most likely to help adaptation while limiting catastrophic forgetting.
engineering_relevance: This offers a principled, parameter-efficient way to continually adapt large language models to new domains without erasing previously learned capabilities.
method: Estimate each channel’s adaptation benefit from domain-specific data.
Use a fixed public general-domain corpus as a proxy for forgetting cost.
Select trainable channels with knee-based screening, Pareto filtering, and Otsu thresholding.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated across four LLM families and eight downstream tasks, where it improves preservation of pretrained knowledge while maintaining strong downstream performance.
watch_item: Channel scoring depends on proxy datasets and thresholding choices, so performance may be sensitive to data selection and implementation details.
paper_title: Stability-Plasticity Balance via Singular-Vector Selection in LLM Continual Learning
